analysis_notes.notes:
Torah LM2/57 contains zero bechina edges in the dataset (reference 1057 is entirely absent from torahData.js). The source text itself — four short paragraphs totalling approximately 80 words — contains no bechina language whatsoever. There is no use of 'בחינת', 'הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', or any structural-identity formula anywhere in the text.

The Torah teaches a single observation about the dynamic between great and small leaders: when a true great Tzaddik (צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל אֲמִתִּי) reveals wondrous Torah novella (חִדּוּשִׁים נִפְלָאִים וְנוֹרָאִים), a great commotion (רַעַשׁ גָּדוֹל) results, and as a consequence everyone gathers to a smaller figure (קָטָן בְּמַעֲלָה) to hear from him. The parallel example of Bilaam — to whom all nations came when God gave the Torah to Israel — illustrates the same mechanism operating within the Sitra Achra.

The entire structure is causal (eitza): great Tzaddik reveals Torah → commotion is created → people gather to the smaller one. The Bilaam example is an illustrative historical parallel, not a bechina equation. No concept in this Torah is said to BE an aspect of another concept; everything is described in terms of what produces what.

Accordingly, no gap additions apply, no unassigned dataset nodes exist, and no concepts from the source text can be flagged as missing from packages (since there are no packages to miss).
